metaDescription: Six Bissell carpet cleaners compared: Big Green, TurboClean uprights, HydroSteam and Little Green portables, with honest notes on who each one suits.
expertTake: The Bissell Big Green Professional is the strongest pick for a home with wall to wall carpet and real traffic, and the TurboClean Pet XL is the sensible upright for most families. The Little Green Mini is the value pick because a small portable solves more daily messes than any big machine. Skip the whole category if your floors are mostly hard surface, because a wet extractor on a few rugs is better rented than owned.
introParagraphs: This maker sells carpet cleaners in three body styles, and the family tree matters more than the model number. Full size uprights wash whole rooms, mid size uprights trade capacity for weight, and small portables with a hose handle stairs, sofas and car seats.

Inside each style the differences come down to tank volume, brush design, hose reach and whether the machine adds heat. This guide sorts the current lineup by what each machine physically does, so you can match the body style to the mess instead of buying on a bundle.

products.name: Bissell Big Green Professional XL DirtLifter
products.description:
The Big Green is the one Bissell that is engineered like a rental machine rather than a household appliance. A 12 amp motor, rotating DirtLifter brushes and a 1.75 gallon clean tank are the specifications that separate it from every other upright in this roundup. It also cleans on both the forward and the backward pass, which matters more than it sounds, because every square foot gets two passes of spray and suction without you doing extra work.

The cost of that capability is mass and bulk. Filled, the machine is a heavy thing to walk up a step, and the 9 inch hose is a short, stiff reach for upholstery rather than a true stair tool. Compared with the TurboClean Pet XL, which is lighter and has a 10 inch path, the Big Green wins on tank volume and brush aggression but loses on hauling convenience.

Plan on rinsing both tanks and pulling the brush rolls after every job, because stored wet they turn sour inside a week. The dirty tank is large, so a full room is a single trip to the drain rather than three. If your carpet is mostly open floor and you clean twice a year, this is the machine that earns its closet space.
products.bestFor: Wall to wall carpet, big rooms and heavy traffic lanes.
pros: Large 1.75 gallon clean tank covers a room per fill
Rotating DirtLifter brushes agitate embedded dirt
Works on both forward and backward passes
12 amp motor gives strong pull for an upright
cons: Heavy and awkward to carry up stairs when full
Short 9 in. hose limits upholstery reach

products.name: Bissell TurboClean Pet XL 3746
products.description:
The Pet XL is built around a wider 10 inch clean path, which is the number that decides how many passes a hallway takes. Larger tanks mean fewer trips to the sink, yet the body stays slimmer than the Big Green, so it still turns in a small bedroom. The 3 inch above floor tool and the included stain tool let it climb onto stairs, baseboards and pet beds.

The trade is raw power. It uses a lighter motor and a less aggressive brush than the Big Green, so oily or years old traffic lane soil may need a second visit. For a family with a dog and a couch, though, the extra reach and lower weight usually matter more than the last bit of agitation.

The tool hose hooks into the upper body and is easy to clog with hair, so pull the stain tool and flush it with clean water after each session. The Pet XL pairs well with the standard TurboClean 3952 as a lower cost option if you do not need the larger tanks.
products.bestFor: Family homes with pets, stairs and a couch to freshen.
pros: Wide 10 in. path means fewer passes per room
XL tanks reduce trips to the sink
Above floor tool covers stairs and pet beds
Lighter and easier to turn than the Big Green
cons: Less brush aggression than the Big Green on old soil
Hair clogs the tool hose if you skip flushing

products.name: Bissell Revolution HydroSteam Pet 3432
products.description:
Heat is the point here. The HydroSteam system warms the wash water, and the SteamWash Max Clean mode is the setting you reach for when the soil is greasy, like kitchen traffic or a food spill that has dried into the pile. Heated water loosens oils that cold water leaves behind, and warm carpet also gives up its moisture faster than a cold wash does.

The tradeoff is complexity and price tier. Heating components add parts, and it sits near the top of the Bissell price range, well above the TurboClean 3952. If your messes are mostly mud and dust, the heat is a cost you do not need.

Use the lower heat setting on wool or delicate fibers, and do the colorfastness spot test in a hidden corner before the first full wash. Descaling is not on the maintenance sheet for a washer this style, but hard water still leaves film on any heating path, so distilled water is a cheap safeguard.
products.bestFor: Greasy kitchen or entry traffic and homes with pets.
pros: Heated wash helps loosen oily and greasy soil
SteamWash Max Clean mode for stubborn areas
2 in 1 pet tool cleans furniture and stairs
Warm water assists faster drying
cons: Higher cost and more parts than a plain upright
Heat settings need care on wool and delicate rugs

products.name: Bissell TurboClean 3952 OXY
products.description:
This is the lowest priced upright in the lineup and the cleanest introduction to the TurboClean design. It ships geared toward an oxygen based formula with a urine eliminator, so out of the box it handles pet accidents without a separate purchase. For a rental cost replacement it is the practical answer.

The compromises are all about scale. With a smaller footprint it holds less water than the Pet XL and the Big Green, and a full living room means refilling partway through. It lacks the HydroSteam heat of the 3432 and the brush strength of the Big Green.

Because the formula system is Bissell specific, follow the manual on which solutions to run, since Bissell manuals say non Bissell formulas can void the warranty. After each use, flush the tanks and leave them open to air dry before storage.
products.bestFor: Occasional deep cleans and a first carpet cleaner purchase.
pros: Lowest price tier among Bissell uprights here
Ships with OXY and urine eliminator formula
Compact footprint stores easily
Familiar TurboClean controls are simple
cons: Smaller tanks mean mid room refills
No heat and a milder brush than the pricier uprights

products.name: Bissell Little Green HydroSteam 3618
products.description:
The HydroSteam Little Green is the portable that adds a third mode to the usual spray and suck cycle. SteamWash handles oily messes, Steam refreshes upholstery and can be used on tile and grout, and Wash is the plain cold cycle. That makes it the only portable in this guide that can double as a small steam cleaner.

It remains a portable, so the water tank is small compared with any upright. The Little Green 1400B and the Mini 4075 are lighter and cheaper if you do not want heat. Expect to refill several times for a single staircase.

Steam on unsealed grout, velvet, silk and similar fabrics can cause damage, so keep the steam mode away from those. After use, run clear water through the hose and leave the tank cap open so the heater passage dries.
products.bestFor: Sofas, stairs and tile where heat helps on grease.
pros: Three modes including a real steam mode
Handles upholstery, stairs and tile grout
Portable weight is easy to carry anywhere
OXY formula suits set in stains
cons: Small tank needs frequent refills on big jobs
Steam is wrong for unsealed grout and delicate fabrics

products.name: Bissell Little Green Mini 4075
products.description:
The Mini trades capacity for a smaller body and one clever feature, the HydroRinse tool. It rinses the hose and tool path with clean water so the dirty residue does not sit and sour in the parts, which is the single most useful bit of upkeep design in the portable class. It is also one of the cheapest machines on the page.

A small body means small tanks and a short job list. It will do sofa cushions, car seats and a landing, but not a staircase and a hallway in one sitting. The standard Little Green 1400B holds more and is a little heavier.

Run the HydroRinse cycle after every use and the machine rarely needs deeper cleaning. Store it with the caps off and the hose draining, then it is ready for the next spill.
products.bestFor: Spills, car seats and sofa cushions on a tight budget.
pros: HydroRinse tool flushes the hose after use
Light and compact to store in a closet
4 in. tough stain tool for tight spots
Among the lowest priced Bissell machines
cons: Small tank is not for whole staircases
Not a replacement for an upright on rooms

buyingCriteria.explanation: An upright washes a room in a few passes, and a portable only does spots, stairs and furniture, so the first decision is the job, not the brand. The Big Green with its 1.75 gallon tank handles a bedroom without a refill, while the Little Green Mini needs refilling for a single staircase. A common buyer mistake is expecting a portable to do whole rooms, which means an hour of refilling and uneven wash lines.

Bigger tanks cover more floor per fill, but water weighs about eight pounds a gallon, so the Big Green at 1.75 gallons adds real mass to carry. The TurboClean Pet XL balances this with a 10 inch path and moderate tanks. If you have stairs between the sink and the job, a mid size upright usually beats the largest one.

Agitation separates a rinse from a clean, and a rotating brush scrubs harder than a fixed one. The Big Green uses rotating DirtLifter brushes with a 12 amp motor, while the portables depend on a hand tool you move by hand. Ignore marketing multipliers and compare brush type and motor amps instead.

Heated wash, as on the HydroSteam 3432 and the Little Green HydroSteam 3618, softens grease that cold water only spreads. Heat is of little use on dust and mud, so it is a poor purchase for a dry household. Keep heat at or under about 140 F on wool and read the care label before steaming.

Stairs and sofas live and die by hose length and the tool in the box. The TurboClean PET family uses a 7 ft hose in its compact line, while the Big Green has a 9 inch reach tool attached to the body. Check which tools ship before comparing, since a missing stain tool is another purchase.

Bissell manuals say non Bissell formulas can void the warranty, so budget for their formulas rather than assuming any detergent works. Low foam matters because foam climbs into the recovery tank and float. Self cleaning features such as the Mini's HydroRinse cut the most common failure, which is a hose clogged with dried residue.

specDecoder.meaning: The volume of clean water plus solution you load before refilling. It sets how much carpet one fill covers.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Big Green's 1.75 gallons is the high mark here, and the Little Green Mini is the low one.

specDecoder.meaning: A 12 amp rating describes electrical draw, not suction in the field. Use it to compare motors from the same maker, not as a cleaning score.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the Big Green lists amps in the data, so compare others by body style.

specDecoder.meaning: How wide a strip the head cleans per pass. Wider means fewer passes and fewer overlap lines.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Pet XL lists a 10 inch path, which is the number to compare with other uprights.

specDecoder.meaning: Bissell's name for a heated wash system that warms the water before it hits the carpet. Heat helps with grease.
specDecoder.watchFor: It appears on the 3432, 4123 and Little Green 3618, and not on the TurboClean 3952.

specDecoder.meaning: What you can reach beyond the floor head. Hose length and the stain tool decide stairs and upholstery work.
specDecoder.watchFor: The TurboClean PET lists a 7 ft hose, while the Big Green has a 9 inch reach tool.

howWeEvaluated.title: Body style fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We sorted every machine by upright, mid size upright and portable, because the style decides what jobs it can do. We evaluated each against stairs, rooms and furniture. A machine that only fits one job was ranked on that job.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tank volume, such as 1.75 gallons on the Big Green against the smaller portables, against how heavy the filled machine is. We weighed trips to the sink against carrying effort. The balance sets the upright ranking.

howWeEvaluated.title: Agitation and heat
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at brush design and whether the model heats the water, with the HydroSteam machines as the heated group. Agitation and heat are what separate a rinse from a clean on tough soil.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tools and reach
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which tools ship, from the 4 inch stain tool on the Mini to the 6 inch stain tool on the Big Green. We evaluated based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns rather than assuming a tool is included.

howWeEvaluated.title: Upkeep and drying
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed how easy each is to flush and store, favoring features like HydroRinse on the Mini. Residue left in a hose causes odor and clogs, so self rinsing design earned credit.

cards.label: Upright
cards.text: The Big Green, TurboClean Pet XL and TurboClean 3952 wash whole rooms in far fewer passes. They need storage space and weigh more when full. They suit anyone with wall to wall carpet.

cards.label: Portable
cards.text: The Little Green Mini and the Little Green HydroSteam 3618 handle spots, stairs and car seats. They fill in seconds but run out of water on big jobs. They suit apartments and spill response.

howToChoose.note: Floors of carpet pick an upright. Spills, stairs and cars pick a portable. Many homes eventually own one of each.

rows: Cold water cleaning only on the standard setup.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A pet specific tool for stairs and bedding, a strong stain formula and a tank that flushes hair easily. Hair clogs the tool hose faster than anything else, so favor machines you can rinse through.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The TurboClean Pet XL 3746 and HydroSteam Pet 3432 are the pet tuned uprights, and the Little Green Mini 4075 covers accidents on furniture with its HydroRinse tool.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have large carpeted areas or heavy traffic, in which case the Big Green's 1.75 gallon tank is worth it. Spend up also if greasy soil is your problem and the HydroSteam 3432 heat is relevant.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You clean once or twice a year, in which case the TurboClean 3952 or the Little Green Mini 4075 does the job without overbuying.

maintenance.why: Dirty water left in the recovery tank sours within days. Rinse and leave caps open to dry.

maintenance.task: Clear and rinse the hose and tool path
maintenance.why: Dried residue and hair block the tool path. On the Mini, run the HydroRinse cycle.
Hair wraps the bristles and reduces agitation. Cut it free with scissors and rinse.

maintenance.task: Check the float and filter screen
maintenance.why: Foam or debris can trip the float and cut suction. Wipe the screen with clean water.

maintenance.task: Use distilled water on heated models
maintenance.why: Minerals scale heating passages over time. Distilled water is a cheap protection.

faq.q: Should I buy a Bissell upright or a Little Green portable?
faq.a: An upright washes whole rooms and a Little Green handles spots, stairs and furniture. If you only have a few rugs, start with a portable like the Mini 4075. If you have wall to wall carpet, an upright such as the TurboClean Pet XL is the better first buy.

faq.q: Is the Big Green worth the extra cost over a TurboClean?
faq.a: It is if your carpet area is large or heavily soiled, because the 1.75 gallon tank and rotating brushes shorten the job. For a small home the TurboClean 3952 does the same work with less to store. Match the machine to the area, not to the badge.

faq.q: Can I use a non Bissell cleaning solution?
faq.a: Bissell manuals say non Bissell formulas can harm the machine and may void the warranty, so check the manual for your model. Low foam is also important, because foam can reach the float and motor. When in doubt use the maker's formula.

faq.q: Does HydroSteam mean the carpet comes out dry?
faq.a: No. Heat helps with grease and warm carpet dries faster than cold wet carpet, but drying still depends on how much water went down and how well it was extracted. Make a dry pass and run fans.

faq.q: How often should I deep clean carpets?
faq.a: Many households clean once or twice a year, with spot cleaning in between. High traffic lanes and pet areas may need more. Overwetting is the bigger risk than infrequent cleaning, because damp pad can lead to mildew.

faq.q: Are the Little Green models safe on upholstery?
faq.a: Generally yes, but test a hidden spot first and avoid soaking the fabric. Steam mode on the HydroSteam 3618 is not for velvet, silk or suede. Always follow the fabric care tag.
